newsitem.title: FINLAND: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Finland key rate cut.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Finland key rate cut.

text.p: Following are analysts' and traders' responses to the Bank of Finland's 15 basis point cut in its key tender rate on Wednesday.

The cut came as the markka has strengthened sharply amid mounting speculation of an imminent link to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), possibly in connection with this weekend's meeting of EU finance and economy ministers in Dublin.
OKOBANK treasury economist Teijo Rantatupa:
"This was a surprise which I would link completely to the strengthening of the markka."
"This will in no way help (weaken the markka), they should have taken off 50 basis points at once, this sort of shaving is not enough."
"But maybe they want to keep their chips in hand for the next few weeks."
"The yield curve will steepen," he said.
Merita chief analyst Jukka Lepomaki:
"This is maybe a small surprise, but it's logical."

"The reasons are clear, this week there has been good data, the inflation outlook is good, everything suggests that there was room for lower rates; and on the foreign exchange market, the bank wants to calm things down."
He said the rate cut had increased expectations that Finland will soon, maybe next weekend, decide on whether or not to link the markka to the ERM. @
"From the market's point of view the important thing is that we could get back to business as usual, whether it would be wise to link the markka to the or not is not important."

"Of course they will talk about it this weekend, it would be stupid not to, but when it will be announced is another thing altogether," he said, adding that an announcement could come on any weekday even if a decision were made next weekend.
He said the cut would probably keep the markka from strengthening more after heavy buying amid central bank intervention brought it below 3.00 on Tuesday. @
"I don't think we will go below 3.00 per mark," he said.
He saw a 3.00 to 3.02 near-term trading range for the markka against the German mark.
Postipankki economist Tarja Heinonen:
"It was not really a surprise because there has been enormous appreciation pressure in the markka ahead of a possible ERM link."
"This morning's producer prices showed the terms of trade deteriorating - so in light of that it was not really a surprise." (The producer price index fell 1.3 percent year on year.)
"I don't think (the Bank of Finland) necessarily wants to weaken it (the markka) but they don't want it to strengthen more." @
Asked if she believed a decision on a link would come this weekend:
"Much depends on financial market reactions to the French budget release -- if that causes turmoil in the markets, it would really be too risky to make an ERM linkage."
Asked what she expected to happen in the markka when foreign exchange trading gets properly underway after 0700 GMT:
"I guess that the appreciation pressure still continue even after this cut," she said.
